page: Amazon Web Services g6.12xlarge is an accelerated computing instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, offering 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. System memory totals 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A central component of this platform is its GPU array, which integrates four NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 accelerators delivering a cumulative 89 GB of VRAM. It also features 3,760 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark data reflects top-tier performance in AI acceleration and parallel compute. Leveraging its four NVIDIA L4 GPUs, the instance reaches top 10% rankings in LLM inference across small, medium, and large model architectures, delivering 12,140.28 tokens/sec prompt processing on 135M models and 2,844.44 tokens/sec on 7B models. Multi-core compute benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, place in the top 25%. However, single-core metrics and system memory bandwidth fall within the middle 50% average range due to DDR4 bus limitations and lack of AVX-512 extensions.

From a qualitative cost perspective, the instance aggregates four enterprise-grade inference GPUs alongside significant NVMe scratch space and dedicated CPU cores into a dense single-node footprint. This structure eliminates distributed cluster management overhead for mid-sized deep learning models. The hardware profile is optimized for generative AI inference, multi-stream real-time video processing, graphics rendering, and batch ML pipelines requiring high-throughput local storage.

Potential tradeoffs involve the lack of advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 or AMX, which shifts heavy compute reliance onto the NVIDIA accelerators. Furthermore, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Amazon Web Services g6.12xlarge is best matched for enterprise LLM deployment, multi-camera computer vision workloads, cloud graphics rendering, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services g6.12xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for AI inference and graphics processing. Powered by a 48-vCPU AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running on the AWS Nitro System, the instance incorporates 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM alongside four NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPUs providing 89 GB of aggregate VRAM. Storage and I/O capacity include 3,760 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 40 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results show top-tier LLM inference execution across various parameter scales, supported by top 25% multi-core processing performance. While single-thread execution and DDR4 memory throughput perform at average levels, the integration of four specialized accelerators makes this configuration suitable for low-latency machine learning serving, multi-stream media processing, and graphics virtualization workloads.
